focus: Busan Political Crisis: military-neutrality refusal chain, martial-law command context, and So Min-ho archive targets

material_findings.finding: The military layer of the Busan Political Crisis cannot be modeled as a single pro-government command chain. AKS biographical records identify Army Chief of Staff Lee Jong-chan as refusing a presidential troop-dispatch demand during the May 1952 crisis; AKS separately records Operations/Education Bureau chief Lee Yong-mun as joining the military-neutrality refusal and later being transferred. This creates an institutionally important opposed_by/refused_by branch inside the armed forces.

AKS's Lee Yong-mun entry ties the neutrality dispute to the May 26 detention of the National Assembly commuter vehicle and records Army Headquarters Directive No.217 ('To Army Soldiers') as the neutrality statement. The exact original directive remains the preferred primary target; later summaries must not substitute for the document text.

NIHK's June 17, 1952 reproduction of the US State Department OIR analysis reports that after the May 25 martial-law phase the Assembly was badly deprived of members through arrest, hiding, unknown whereabouts and boycott. This is a contemporaneous foreign analytical observation and should not be silently converted into a Korean judicial finding or exact arrest roster.

NIHK's overseas-archives catalog gives a precise NARA Box 15 target for the So Min-ho trial: Summary of the So Min Ho Trial, National Assembly special-investigation reports Nos.1-3, USIS courtroom photographs, June 20 trial photographs, and UN GA A/AC.39/INF.117. The catalog also names the six members of the May 9 special investigation committee: Yu Hong, Kim Gwang-jun, Jo Sun, Kim Jeong-gi, Jo Jeong-hun and Lee Seok-gi. These names are candidate political nodes, but committee membership still needs identity disambiguation before registry promotion.

Rhee's June 25 letter to Truman is preserved in the NIHK FRUS layer with provenance to the Truman Library White House central files. It explicitly presents Rhee's own defense that reports about the Busan disturbances were distorted. This is a high-value adversarial source because it preserves the principal actor's counter-narrative and must be stored as party assertion, not neutral adjudication.

Kim Seong-su's AKS biography records his May 29 resignation from the vice presidency in protest against the May 26 political crisis. This adds a constitutionally senior opposed_by actor and a distinct resignation sub-event rather than treating elite opposition as an undifferentiated bloc.

adversarial_checks: Military institutions were not modeled as uniformly compliant; Lee Jong-chan and Lee Yong-mun's refusal line is preserved.
Rhee's June 25 defense to Truman is preserved as the principal actor's assertion rather than discarded because it conflicts with foreign reporting.
OIR's use of coup-like analytical framing is not converted into a Korean court finding.
The June 17 OIR headcount categories are not treated as a verified individual arrest roster.
Won Yong-deok's 1952 operational role is not inferred solely from his later career as provost marshal/MP commander.
Directive No.217 is not quoted from secondary summaries before its original text is opened.
Committee-member names from the NARA catalog are not promoted to stable politicians until same-name identities are resolved.
Kim Seong-su's resignation is separated from the May 25 proclamation and May 26 detention as its own political act.
Foreign diplomatic/analytical observations and Korean domestic legal acts remain separate provenance families.
The So Min-ho archive catalog is treated as an archival finding aid, not as proof of the contents of unopened reports Nos.1-3.
